question: Are the remaining active-check families (SQLi, reflected/stored XSS & DOM, open redirect, header injection, SSTI, OS command, LDAP, code injection, SMTP, server-level, external interaction, header manipulation) implemented with Burp's actual payloads, detection logic and confirmation steps, or only matched to Burp by family name?
probes: For each family: map family -> check class via /root/burp-re/out/names/*.tsv (FilePathTraversalCheck -> Zp3a pattern), read its control flow in out/clean/pristine, decode its literal tables by loading /root/burp-re/in/extract/burp classes with /tmp/wave31-evidence/Walk.java-style reflection, then port payloads + detection + confirmation into scan.rs with pure-function tests and an end-to-end scan test.
Port burp.Zw4k.ZI (ignore marker matches inside ASP.NET viewstate) for the file-read checks.

SMTP header injection is now ported (fnd_48). Remaining name-only families and their Burp classes: SqlAndXPathInjectionCheck=Zg_c, XssAndTemplateInjectionCheck=Zi6p, OpenRedirectionCheck=Zuag, HttpResponseHeaderInjectionCheck=Zwi, OsCommandInjectionCheck=Zx8l, LdapInjectionCheck=Zwkf, CodeInjectionCheck=Zsn3 (+ServerSideJavaScriptInjectionCheck=Zg_v), TraceMethodEnabledCheck=Zs6x, InputRetrievalReflectedCheck=Zr02, XmlInjectionInsertionPointCheck=Zp7s, CollaboratorEverywhereCheck=Zc7h; Burp also has ServerSideIncludeInjectionCheck=Zexx (no WebProbe family yet). Insertion-point payload modes are known: burp.Ziqd.ZT mode 0 = replace value, mode 1 = base value + payload.

SQLi remaining from burp.Zppj: error-based variant (Zppj.ZE; signature strings encrypted, decode via in/extract classes), time-based (Zppj.ZT), backslash-powered differences (Zeyh.FIND_BACKSLASH_POWERED_SCANNING_DIFFERENCES); resolve Zgx0.ZO()/Zs() (Ziqf.Zz.Zc()) to confirm the unquoted-attempt gate.

Time-based payload library located (decode next): burp.Zuyg MSSQL waitfor delay, burp.Zxpy PostgreSQL pg_sleep, burp.Zxom OS command ping (-n/-c %% 127.0.0.1), plus Zbyb/Zfhw/Zcw5/Zm4e/Zxbc builders; prefixes in Ze2s; timing engine burp.Zwj_ (mostly undecompilable, read bytecode). These replace WebProbe's ';sleep 3' OS-command and SQL time probes.
Use the live Burp REST harness (/tmp/burp-api, /tmp/parity-lab) as the acceptance test for every family: Burp's issue list for the lab must equal WebProbe's (names, severity, confidence).

XssAndTemplateInjectionCheck burp.Zi6p map: (a) Zw7s step FIND_XSS_REFLECTED fills Zx5c with context results; ZI reports client-side breakout. (b) Server-side breakout iterates burp.Zch1 closers: '}}', '%}', rand5+'%>' at FAST+, and '%]', rand5+';//';//";//%>?>' at THOROUGH, through burp.Zf5z/Zg7k. (c) Template engines burp.Znq decision tree, gated on Zw7s.ZH() plain reflection: Zwr2/Zbdb combinators over Zsl3, Zbrp, Zbhh (expression language), Zf8q, Zh9k, Zhcj, Zbb6, Zp1w, Zhuy, Ziyq, Zxpo, Zieh, Zf9k, Zpk0, Zh3a, Zi1a, Zpjg, Zgok. At THOROUGH or with prior XSS: Zsr_, Zbd4, Zu86, Zwbu, Zc69, Zx70, Zhte. (d) Collaborator-based SSTI burp.Zp3p (THOROUGH or minimise false negatives). Port each detector with its decoded literals; replace WebProbe's {{7*7}}/${7*7} name-only probes.

Link manipulation (reflected), burp.Zb_5 (444 lines, mostly bytecode): covers LINK_MANIPULATION, CLIENT_SIDE_HTTP_PARAMETER_POLLUTION, FORM_ACTION_HIJACKING, CSS_INJECTION (reflected/stored) via Zcpt.Zb reflection contexts; port after XSS context analysis exists.
Done in waves 39-40 and verified on the live lab: HTTP response header injection (Zwi), Input returned in response (reflected) (Zr02).

XSS engine blueprint (burp.Zgkd -> Zguu -> Zglf): Zp12.ZJ iterates the 26 reflection contexts. Per context: APPEND reflection, then REPLACE (always for contexts 7-11), then decoding-variant reflections (Zguu.Zm). A reflection classified in context c (Zh38.ZB(2,c), finder burp.Zfpy(c)) goes to Zglf.Zz -> breakout handler Zglf.Zt(c): 0/19 Zbio|Zw2t HTML text; 2,3,7 Zszd; 4/5/6 Zuce(" ' `) quoted attribute values; 8/9/10 Zm6x(" ' `) JS strings; 11 Zw4x JS code; 12/13/14 Ziki(" ' `); 15 Ziz1; 16/17 Zh7u(" ') quoted URL attributes; 18 Zms5; 20/21/22 Zudy xmp/noscript/title; 23 Zxk8; 24/25 Zhoc('\n','*/') JS comments. Encoding probes come from Zglf.ZX through Zcyd = Zbno(Zb43, Zepw, Zmap, Zplz). Port order: context classifier (Zfpy), then each handler's payload literals (decode with Zkm.java/Statics.java), then the Zpbh evaluator.

XSS breakout handlers (wave 42 start): Zglf.Zt handlers are trees over 76 burp.Zuw7 classes. Combinators: burp.Zpx4 = sequence (each step must succeed, the level is passed on via Zpbh.Zv), burp.Ziul = first success.
